title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 101
paragraphs: Moreover, this other coincidence occurred besides: a sacred precinct of Eleusinian Demeter stood close beside both battlefields. Not only in the Plataean land did the fight take place close beside the temple of Demeter, as I have said, but in Mycale too it was to be the same. And the rumor that reached them — that a victory had already been won by the Greeks with Pausanias — proved to be a true report; for what happened at Plataea came about while it was still early morning, but the fighting at Mycale took place in the afternoon. That it happened on the same day of the same month as the other became evident to them not long afterwards, when they inquired into the matter. Before the rumor arrived, they had been afraid — not so much for themselves as for the Greeks in general, lest Greece should stumble and fall over Mardonius. But when this report came suddenly to them, they advanced on the enemy much more vigorously and swiftly than before. Both Greeks and barbarians were going eagerly into the battle, since the islands and the Hellespont were placed before them as prizes of the contest.
